prompt: Euclid replaces a pair of non-negative integers with the divisor and remainder, stopping before division by zero. Why does this preserve the gcd?

options.text: The two numbers always keep the same sum.
The remainder must itself already be the gcd.
Every smaller number divides the larger one.
options.explanation: The algorithm is needed precisely when division can leave a remainder.

options.text: A divisor common to either pair also divides the other pair.
options.explanation: Subtracting or adding whole multiples preserves common divisibility.

workedExample: A common divisor of the original two numbers divides their difference after subtracting any whole multiple. Conversely, a divisor shared by the divisor and remainder divides the original number reconstructed from them. Thus the set of common divisors is unchanged. Positive remainders shrink until zero is reached.
